actions.name: LockBit affiliates attacked organizations across critical infrastructure sectors
actions.description: Since January 2020, affiliates using LockBit have attacked organizations of varying sizes across an array of critical infrastructure sectors, including financial services, food and agriculture, education, energy, government and emergency services, healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation.

actions.name: LockBit ransomware operation functions as a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model
actions.description: LockBit ransomware operation functions as a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model where affiliates are recruited to conduct ransomware attacks using LockBit ransomware tools and infrastructure.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates use various freeware and open-source tools for malicious cyber activity
actions.description: During their intrusions, LockBit affiliates have been observed using various freeware and open-source tools that are intended for legal use. When repurposed by LockBit, these tools are then used for a range of malicious cyber activity, such as network reconnaissance, remote access and tunneling, credential dumping, and file exfiltration.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates exploit multiple CVEs for initial access and privilege escalation
actions.description: LockBit affiliates have been documented exploiting numerous CVEs, including CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-22986, CVE-2020-1472, CVE-2019-0708, and CVE-2018-13379.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates perform double extortion by encrypting and exfiltrating victim data
actions.description: Since 2021, LockBit affiliates have employed double extortion by first encrypting victim data and then exfiltrating that data while threatening to post that stolen data on leak sites.

actions.name: LockBit 3.0 affiliates disable EDR and antivirus processes and services
actions.description: LockBit 3.0 affiliates use Backstab, Defender Control, GMER, PCHunter, PowerTool, Process Hacker or TDSSKiller to disable EDR processes and services.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates use batch scripts to bypass PowerShell execution policy
actions.description: LockBit 3.0 affiliates use Bat Armor to bypass the PowerShell execution Policy.

actions.name: LockBit 3.0 deletes log files and clears Windows Event Logs
actions.description: LockBit 3.0 deletes log files and empties the recycle bin and clears the Windows Event Logs files.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates use stolen or brute forced credentials for initial access and lateral movement
actions.description: LockBit affiliates obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining initial access and may leverage VPN or RDP brute force credentials.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates perform lateral movement using remote desktop software and SMB shares
actions.description: LockBit affiliates use Splashtop remote-desktop software and may use Cobalt Strike and target SMB shares for lateral movement.

actions.name: LockBit affiliates exfiltrate data using custom and publicly available tools
actions.description: LockBit affiliates use StealBit, a custom exfiltration tool, and publicly available file sharing services such as FileZilla, Rclone, FreeFileSync, and MEGA for data exfiltration.

actions.name: LockBit 3.0 encrypts data on target systems and deletes volume shadow copies
actions.description: LockBit 3.0 encrypts data on target systems to interrupt availability to system and network resources and deletes volume shadow copies residing on disk.

actions.name: LockBit 3.0 changes host system wallpaper and icons to LockBit branding
actions.description: LockBit 3.0 changes the host system’s wallpaper and icons to the LockBit 3.0 wallpaper and icons, respectively.
